body:
# Independent audit: three fibers with only the middle centrally symmetric

Source fully audited:
`candidate b13e43ee6ee1d8af`,
Sections 1–6. Result: PASS, with exactly three positive full-dimensional
fibers and symmetry of the middle fiber retained as explicit hypotheses.

## 1. Actual residual geometry and every ambient halfspace

The source's endpoint traces have thresholds (u\cdot c+\alpha) and
\(u\cdot c-\alpha\), so their closed residuals have Minkowski midpoint
inside the SAME missed middle half. This inclusion is correct for every
finite integer tilt and every nonzero continuous normal (u). Boundary
hyperplanes have zero full-dimensional fiber volume, so closed captured
and residual masses add exactly to each endpoint's total.

If total normalized endpoint capture (P<a\le1), both residual bodies
have positive volume. Ordinary Brunn–Minkowski therefore applies without
discarding an empty or lower-dimensional residual. For fixed (P), the
root-sum function is concave in the allocation (U\in[0,P]). Its smaller
endpoint puts ALL captured mass into the smaller endpoint fiber; the
source's decreasing-increment argument proves the orientation, including
the equality case (d=1). Thus

\[
(a-P)^{1/d}+1\le2h^{1/d}
\]

and the all-status lower bound

\[
P\ge\bigl(a-(2h^{1/d}-1)_+^d\bigr)_+
\]

follow exactly. If (P\ge a), the bound is automatic; if (2h^{1/d}\le1),
the positive-residual alternative is impossible. No supporting or empty
cut status is assumed away.

Pure integer halfspaces through the actual middle point capture the whole
middle and at least the smaller endpoint. This exceeds the displayed
nonvertical bound. Parallel shrinking handles arbitrary containing closed
halfspaces. The larger endpoint centroid is an actual mixed point and its
own fiber supplies (b\Gamma_d) in every ambient orientation.

## 2. Exact scalar optimization

The claimed uniform coefficient is

\[
\beta_d=\frac{\Gamma_d}{1+2\Gamma_d+\rho_d},\qquad
\rho_d=\left(\frac{d-1}{d+1}\right)^d.
\]

The scalar proof covers all (a\in[0,1]), (h\ge0), even beyond the
geometrically needed volume domain. For (h\le\Gamma_d), the single
breakpoint (a_0=\Gamma_d-h+s^d\) belongs to ([0,1]). The constant
branch decreases and the affine branch increases as functions of (a),
with derivative numerator (1+h+s^d>0), so the minimum occurs exactly
there. For \(\Gamma_d\le h\le1\), it occurs at (a=s^d\).

The inverse relation (h=2^{-d}(1+(s^d)^{1/d})^d\) is concave by its
finite positive power expansion. Its comparison with the affine chord
through \((\rho_d,\Gamma_d)\) is correctly oriented and proves the
second regime. For (h\ge1\), the lower bound (1/4\) suffices.

The binomial identity

\[
(d+1)^d-(d-1)^d
=2\sum_{j\ {
m odd}}\binom dj d^{d-j}\ge2d^d
\]

has equality exactly at (d=1,2); it proves
\(2\Gamma_d+\rho_d\le1\) and the strict coefficient improvement for
every (d\ge3\). In particular \(\beta_1=1/4\), \(\beta_2=2/9\), and
\(\beta_3=3/14\) are correct. The scalar equality descriptions are
properly separated from claims of geometric equality.

## 3. Measure, deterministic selection, and realizability

All measures are sums of ordinary (d)-volumes over exactly the three
integer bases. Thus (q=d\), every mass is finite and positive, and no
ambient ((d+1))-volume is substituted. Dividing by (b\) rescales every
term uniformly; exchanging endpoints is the lattice-preserving reflection
of the one integer coordinate. The rule comparing (L\) with \(\Gamma_d\)
selects one deterministic point from the two actual fibers.

Compatibility \((A+B)/2\subset K\) makes the three-layer convex hull have
exactly these fibers; all are full-dimensional and the resulting body has
nonempty ambient interior. The argument does not extend its conclusion to
additional integer bases or lower-dimensional positive intrinsic fibers.

## 4. Exact planar two-center sharpness

For (B=\operatorname{conv}((-1,0),(1,0),(0,1))\), (A=B/3\), and
\(K=\operatorname{conv}((2/3)B,-(2/3)B)\), the volumes are
\(1,1/9,8/9\) and total two. The downward through-center cap captures
only null endpoint boundary edges and exactly (4/9\) of the middle.
The larger endpoint centroid cap has area (4/9\); integer tilt one
excludes both other fibers strictly. Hence both selected points have raw
depth exactly (4/9\), giving normalized (2/9\).

This is sharpness of the specified two-point selector. It makes no
unsupported claim about the global maximum depth of that example.

## 5. Appended cone sharpness in every dimension

The all-dimensional extension of Section 5 also passes. With symmetric
base (D\) of \((d-1)\)-volume (d\), the cone with height one has volume
one and axial centroid (1/(d+1)\). Its apex cap through that centroid has
volume (\Gamma_d\). The proposed scaled endpoint has volume \(\rho_d\),
and the double cone middle has volume (2\Gamma_d\).

The equality (K=rB\cup(-rB)\) uses symmetry of the base explicitly:
its section at height (q\) is \((r-|q|)D\). This nonnegative concave
radial profile indeed defines a convex body, so no gap between the union
and the stated convex hull is present. The downward middle cap captures
only null endpoint bases, and integer tilt one isolates the apex cap at
the larger endpoint centroid. Both actual raw depths are exactly
\(\Gamma_d\), proving sharpness for the specified two-center selection.

The separate interval family has total mass (2(1+a)\), middle-center raw
depth \((1+a)/2\), and endpoint-centroid raw depth (1/2\). It therefore
attains coefficient (1/4\) for every (a\in(0,1]\). None of these claims
identifies the global best point, which the source correctly leaves open.

The expanded exact verifier was rerun independently and passed all 16,989 checks.
The result rigorously repairs the earlier density-only two-certificate
failure by retaining actual residual geometry, but remains a scoped
three-fiber symmetry theorem rather than unrestricted OC.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
